text:
Marta: quick follow-up on the client-side provisional credits PoC — posting observations and questions. RFC linked: https://redwood/rfcs/edge-provisional-credits (draft) :eyes:
Vikram: saw the doc, thanks. can you summarize the main tradeoffs you found during the PoC?
Marta: sure. TL;DR: client hints + local soft-reservations reduce tail by ~15% during short bursts, but increase central visibility complexity and makes billing attribution fuzzier.
Jonah: where does the complexity show up?
Marta: two places: 1) telemetry - we need client tags on every admission decision (trace propagation + token id), 2) fairness - local reservations can allow noisy clients to hoard short windows unless we add decay/backpressure.
Ashley: for telemetry, can we attach a stable trace id early (x-client-credit-id) and carry it through the admission path? seems cheap.
Vikram: yep, but it means changing SDKs and edge proxies. We need a migration plan (old SDKs -> no tag). fallback semantics?
Marta: PoC did this: SDK emits header X-Credit-Stamp if available, edge proxy attaches admission_blob and emits metric: quota.provisional.request{client_id, stamped=true/false}.
Marta: sample metric names and logs from PoC:
```
# histogram of provisional reservation hold times (ms)
quota.provisional.hold_time_ms.bucket: [0,10,50,100,250,1000,inf]
quota.provisional.request.count: int
quota.provisional.reject.count: int
# log line example
INFO quota_admit id=abc123 client=tenant-a provisional=true hold_ms=32 route=/v1/generate
```
Jonah: nice. Did the PoC show any SLO regressions for non-provisional requests?
Marta: negligible (<1% p99 shift) in our synthetic burst test. But we saw 5-7% higher CPU on admission path due to extra metadata handling when stamping enabled.
Oliver: what's the abuse surface? can malicious clients generate many stamped tokens and fake locality to bypass central quotas?
Marta: good catch. We added a cheap stamp signing using the edge's key (HMAC) so central can verify authenticity. SDK can't forge without a key. But that pushes signing into proxy/edge layer.
Vikram: then we need key rotation and latency budget for signing. Did PoC measure HMAC cost?
Marta: signing added ~0.4ms per request in baseline. On heavy bursts it's ~5% of admission CPU.
Ashley: tradeoff seems acceptable if we gate with a rollout toggle. Also we should consider sampling stamps for low-risk clients to reduce cost.
Jonah: another angle: what about billing and unit accounting? provisional holds might produce double-counting windows if not reconciled.
Marta: PoC reconciles on completion: when tokens consumed we emit quota.usage.consume with credit_stamp_id and source=provisional|central. reconciliation job de-dupes by stamp id.
Oliver: de-dupe job adds another ingestion path. Need retention policy for stamps to limit storage.
Marta: PoC retains stamps 7 days, that's enough to reconcile most long-running requests. we can shorten to 24-48h in practice.
Vikram: rollout plan idea: 1) opt-in tenants (small cohort) 2) enable header stamping at edge 3) soft admit (still count centrally) 4) enable reconciliation and billed-from-stamp 5) wider rollout. timeline?
Marta: PoC timeline estimate: 6 weeks end-to-end with one engineer + infra help.
Ashley: dependency list: SDK changes, edge proxy sign hook, admission service header verification, reconciliation ingestion path, metrics dashboards + alerting. Also update billing pipeline.
InfraBot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood/tasks/6421 (status: open) :pushpin:
Vikram: tests we need: stress (mixed tenancies), forged-stamp injection, latency microbench for signing, telemetry completeness check (histograms + traces).
Jonah: for fairness, propose adding decay window: local provisional credit budgets leak back to central over 10s if unused. prevents hoarding.
Marta: implemented leak in PoC as leaky-bucket with rate = central_alloc * 0.2 per second; adjustable.
Oliver: that sounds heuristic-y. we should capture failure modes in RFC appendix with simulation plots.
Marta: agreed — I'll add sim results and a short comparison matrix (cost, latency, abuse risk, rollout complexity).
Ashley: also add a pluggable knob: stamping_strategy = {always, sampled, tenant-only} so ops can reduce surface.
Vikram: OK. next actions: Marta to update RFC with telemetry names, sampling strategies, key-rotation plan, and rollout checklist. Jonah/Oliver to draft SRE runbook for reconciliation failures. Ashley to spec SDK header ergonomics. I'll coordinate canary tenants.
Marta: thanks — I'll push updates by EOD and ping this thread. :rocket:
Jonah: thanks all.
InfraBot: deployment ticket 6421 updated by Marta (assignee: Vikram)
